journal.name: 2023 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics Europe & European Quantum Electronics Conference (CLEO/Europe-EQEC)

data.abstract: Due to the significantly increased peak electric field of available terahertz (THz) pulses, various THz-driven particle accelerators and manipulators have been demonstrated in the last decade, such as THz pulse driven waveguide structure [1], inverse free-electron laser [2] and electron accelerator and manipulator [3]. Recently we have proposed a table-top electron accelerator setup powered by THz pulses, in which the electron source was a krypton gas jet [4]. In our numerical model we have simulated the whole physical process and considered the ionization procedure combining with the THz induced electron acceleration. The model shows a significant influence of the ionization on acceleration mechanisms.

journal.name: 2021 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics Europe & European Quantum Electronics Conference (CLEO/Europe-EQEC)

data.abstract: Two-color laser filamentation constitute one of the most convenient and efficient sources of pulsed ultra-broadband terahertz (THz) radiation. In this approach, a Gaussian ultrashort laser pulse together with its second harmonic are focused into a gas medium, forming a filament, which emits THz radiation with extremely high THz electric and magnetic fields [1] . A major advantage of two-color filamentation is that one can tune the emitted THz radiation in terms of energy, spectrum, polarization and THz beam divergence by properly tailoring the filament itself [2] , [3] . One way to achieve this tailoring is with the use of robust exotic-wavepackets from the family of accelerating beams such as the ring-Airy and the 2D Airy beams. Two-color plasma channels induced by pre-engineered abruptly autofocusing ring-Airy beams have already been proposed in order to enhance the THz yield by 5.3 times compared to a Gaussian-beam-induced plasma [4] .

journal.name: 2021 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics Europe & European Quantum Electronics Conference (CLEO/Europe-EQEC)

data.abstract: Terahertz (THz) frequency radiation has recently drawn special attention due to its broad applications and a unique nature [1] . One of the sources generating a strong signal of such waves is an air plasma induced by focused bichromatic femtosecond laser pulses. Since in this case conversion efficiency of THz radiation generation is quite low, but the risk of damaging active medium practically does not exist, usually during the generation pump pulse energy is increased to as high as possible. This brings a variety of nonlinear effects including a temporal pulse reshaping into the action. However a good spatial and temporal overlap of bichromatic pump pulses is crucial for the efficient THz radiation generation. Note that in the common experimental setups a single focused bichromatic beam is used for the plasma creation, which eliminates the possibility to vary initial time delay between the fundamental and the second laser harmonics. Therefore here we present the results of an experiment where we demonstrate a strong interrelation between generation efficiency of THz radiation and both the time delay between the bichromatic pump pulses and their energies.
